# The desktop container, taskbar and app window move into src

## Context

Leaf of #21198 that completes the shell. After #21199 (the window manager) and #21200 (the launcher and its apps tree), the demo still owns the pieces that put them together: `view/Desktop.mjs` (the workspace), `view/Taskbar.mjs` with the start button, `view/TaskList.mjs`, and `view/AppWindow.mjs`.

## The Problem

Without these pieces in `src/`, a consumer still assembles the shell by copying the demo, and the window manager has no owner but a consumer's controller.

## The Architectural Reality

- Design authority: n/a — moves and generalizes existing behavior; calls none of it wrong.
- `AppWindow` is a `dialog.Base` that grows out of its launcher icon (`animateTargetId`), stays inside the workspace (`boundaryContainerId`, `resizablePluginConfig`), and fires `headerAction` for minimize. Today its opener hands it a state provider with `data.app`, parented to the desktop's (`ViewportController.mjs:80`), and it binds `title: data => data.app.text`.
- The taskbar is a `toolbar.Base`. Its start button's `menu.List` reads the same apps store as the launcher, so every submenu honors the filter (#21062).
- Below 600px the taskbar shows icons only and windows fill the workspace; the demo's SCSS holds that.
- Styles: `resources/scss/src/apps/webdesktop/{AppWindow,Desktop,TaskList,Taskbar}.scss`, with neo-dark and neo-light variables.
- The window controls (from #21272): `dialog.Base#maximize` toggles `maximized` and swaps the button's icon between `maximizeCls` and `minimizeCls` (`src/dialog/Base.mjs:648-654`). `minimizeCls` is `far fa-window-minimize` (`src/dialog/Base.mjs:122-124`), the glyph the demo also uses for its real Minimize (`apps/webdesktop/view/AppWindow.mjs:62`), so a maximized demo window shows two identical buttons. An icon-only action's accessible name comes from its action name once, at creation (`src/toolbar/Base.mjs:717-723`), so the toggled button stays "maximize". A consumer's `headerConfig.actions` replaces the default list (`src/dialog/header/Toolbar.mjs:17-35`, spread in `src/dialog/Base.mjs:548-558`).

## The Fix

- `src/desktop/AppWindow.mjs`: the dialog, with minimize, maximize and close. Its public input is a `record` config (title and icon come from it); any state provider stays internal. Its `@summary` carries the naming rule of #21198 and points at `Neo.manager.Window`.
- `src/desktop/TaskList.mjs`: a list over the tasks store; a click restores the window or brings it to the front through the manager.
- `src/desktop/Taskbar.mjs`: the start button with a `menu.List` over the apps store, the task list, and room for a consumer's own items (the demo's account chip, theme and permissions buttons).
- `src/desktop/Container.mjs`: the workspace, launcher and taskbar. It creates and owns the `Neo.desktop.WindowManager`, whose `windowClass` defaults to `Neo.desktop.AppWindow`, loaded lazily.
- `examples/desktop/basic`: three apps, no sign-in, built from `Neo.desktop.Container` and a `Neo.desktop.store.Apps` with no controller code of its own. It uses the family's launcher (#21200) and brings none of its own, so it tests every seam a consumer touches. It is the family's second consumer, the guide's source (#21202) and the theme leaf's surface (#21205).
- The demo's viewport becomes its sign-in plus a `Neo.desktop.Container`. Its controller keeps sign-in, permissions and theme, and hands the container the manager's `reset()` on sign-out.
- Styles move to `resources/scss/src/desktop/` with the neo-dark and neo-light variables, the phone layout included. The other three themes are #21205.
- The maximize toggle in `dialog.Base` shows a restore glyph and updates the button's accessible name with the state.

## Contract Ledger

| Target Surface | Source of Authority | Proposed Behavior | Fallback | Docs | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Neo.desktop.Container` (owns a `WindowManager`; configs for its stores and window class) | #21198 | One component a consumer drops in for a working desktop | Without an apps store it renders an empty workspace | JSDoc | e2e on `examples/desktop/basic` |
| `Neo.desktop.AppWindow#record` | #21198 (Mnemosyne's review) | The window's only public input; title and icon follow it | Without a record it renders an empty, untitled window | JSDoc | unit |
| `Neo.desktop.AppWindow` (`headerAction` minimize, maximize, close) | the demo's `AppWindow` | As the demo behaves today | — | JSDoc | e2e |
| `Neo.desktop.Taskbar` (consumer item slot), `Neo.desktop.TaskList` | the demo's views | As the demo behaves today | — | JSDoc | e2e |
| `dialog.Base` maximize toggle (restore glyph, accessible name) | #21272 | The restore state shows a restore glyph; the name reads "maximize" or "restore" | — | JSDoc | unit |

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: The four classes exist under `src/desktop/` with `@summary` JSDoc, and the container owns the window manager.
- [ ] AC-2: `examples/desktop/basic` ships: three apps, no sign-in, no controller code of its own. An e2e spec on it opens an app, minimizes it, restores it from the taskbar, brings one of two windows to the front, and closes it.
- [ ] AC-3: The styles live under `resources/scss/src/desktop/` with the neo-dark and neo-light variables, the phone layout included; the demo keeps none of the shell's styles.
- [ ] AC-4: The demo is unchanged for its user: `test/playwright/e2e/webdesktop/PhoneAndTouch.spec.mjs` and the demo's unit specs pass, and its viewport holds only sign-in, the container and its own taskbar items.
- [ ] AC-5 (#21272): An app window shows Minimize, Maximize/Restore and Close without consumer handlers. A maximized window shows a restore glyph, distinct from Minimize, and the button's accessible name follows the state.
- [ ] AC-6 (#21272): Minimize, then a restore from the taskbar, and Maximize, then Restore, both return the window to its normal size and position.
- [ ] AC-7 (#21272): A consumer changes one control's icon without losing the others and can leave out a single control; the guide (#21202) shows both. Minimize appears only on windows a manager can restore.

## Out of Scope

The guide (#21202); the cyberpunk, dark and light themes (#21205); a window in its own browser window (D#21204); more than one window per app.

6. **The demo.** Its viewport becomes sign-in plus `Neo.desktop.Container`. Its controller keeps the sign-in, which hands the launcher its key before the grants, the sign-out (manager reset, grants, key null), the permissions and the theme.

Two choices the review should know:
- **Minimize is the window manager's contribution** to each window it creates (`toolbar.Base#addActionContribution`), not an `AppWindow` action, so it appears only on windows a manager can restore, whatever their class. A header that drops it from its vocabulary (`actionMap: {minimize: null}`) gets none.
- **Maximize is a `Neo.toolbar.ActionButton` toggle**, the primitive the dock's maximize uses: `maximized` presses it, and its glyph and accessible name ("maximize" or "restore") follow.

Pending outside this leaf: the desktop family row in the Portal's examples list waits for #21309, which rewrites that list. When the leaves land, these commits go onto `dev` and the pull request opens.
